subject: Critical Thinking
title: René Descartes: Doubting Everything to Find Certainty
description: A short lesson to help you apply René Descartes: Doubting Everything to Find Certainty.

hook.text: 'I think, therefore I am.' The most famous sentence in philosophy.

buildup.text: Descartes' method: doubt everything. Senses deceive, math might be wrong, reality could be a dream.

discovery.text: Only one thing: the act of doubting itself proves a doubter exists.

twist.text: His rebuilding was less successful – he needed God to guarantee truth, which many found unconvincing.

climax.text: Cartesian doubt lives on: in science, in philosophy, and in daily life.

punchline.text: He doubted everything and found the one undoubtable truth: doubt itself.

quiz.question: What is Descartes' method of systematic doubt?
options: Doubting all beliefs until finding something that cannot be doubted

details.summary: René Descartes attempted to doubt everything that could possibly be doubted, arriving at 'I think, therefore I am' as the one undeniable truth. His method of radical doubt became the foundation of modern philosophy and scientific skepticism.
details.whyItMatters: Descartes showed that genuine certainty requires systematic doubt. His method remains the philosophical basis for questioning assumptions before accepting any claim.
takeaways: Descartes methodically doubted all beliefs to find certainty
Cogito ergo sum survived every attempted doubt
His method established systematic doubt as a philosophical tool

faq.question: What exactly is Descartes' method of radical doubt?
faq.answer: Descartes imagined that everything he believed could be false — his senses might deceive him, he might be dreaming, an evil demon might be manipulating his thoughts. Only the act of doubting itself proved something existed: the doubter.

faq.question: What are the main criticisms of Descartes' approach to knowledge?
faq.answer: Critics argue his method leads to solipsism, that his jump from 'I think' to establishing the external world requires assumptions he claims to have eliminated, and that his reliance on God to guarantee truth is circular.
